title: Syncthing on Retro Handhelds! Save Sync Guide
summary: Retro Game Corps demonstrates Syncthing as a way to synchronize emulator saves across handhelds, with a written guide and attention to device-specific paths.
searchKeywords: Syncthing on Retro Handhelds! Save Sync Guide

blocks.text: Moving between handhelds is easy only when both systems agree on where a game stores progress. This guide sets up Syncthing for RetroArch saves and save states on several operating systems, then shows how a completed session on one device can appear on another over a local network. Its written companion is useful for checking the exact folder paths after watching the demonstration. The concept is portable even when a particular device menu has changed.

Treat synchronization as replication, not as a backup by itself. Before connecting two devices, preserve a separate copy of their save folders and choose one authoritative version for the first sync. Avoid running the same game on both devices while files are changing, because a conflict can overwrite newer progress. In-game saves and emulator states have different compatibility requirements; matching core, game revision and state format matters. Test with a disposable save before entrusting a long playthrough to the workflow.
